title: Man Dies After Biting Into Explosive Disguised as Rasgulla; Two Arrested in India
excerpt: Rajendra Barautiya, 35, died in Madhya Pradesh after biting into a crude boar-hunting explosive disguised as a rasgulla. Police have arrested two men and charged them with culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

A 35-year-old man in India died after biting into a homemade explosive disguised as a rasgulla, a traditional syrup-soaked sweet, and police have arrested two men in connection with his death, according to reports.

Rajendra Barautiya, 35, an agricultural laborer, was gathered with others around a bonfire on Tuesday night, November 10, in Dindori district, in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, when a fellow villager handed him what looked like a rasgulla, according to police and news reports. Believing it was an ordinary sweet, Barautiya put it in his mouth and bit down. The device detonated, inflicting catastrophic facial and jaw injuries. He was rushed to a hospital, where he died.

Police identified the villager who handed him the device as Ramabhagat Barautiya. The device was a crude boar-hunting explosive — a ball of dough packed with gunpowder, often sourced from firecrackers or quarry stock — of the kind some rural communities use to kill wild boars. “The bomb, used by some tribal people in the area to kill wild boars, was offered to this man. It exploded in his mouth,” police officer Rekha Singh told reporters.

Two men have been arrested and charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, according to reports. Police said the investigation remains ongoing, including how the device was obtained and whether the handover was deliberate.

All charges are allegations, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; Al Jazeera, citing AFP; CBS News; Air News.
